patch.sql:
select
    c.customer_key,
    c.customer_name,
    c.market_segment,
    c.account_balance,
    n.nation_name,
    r.region_name
from {{ ref('stg_customers') }} c
join {{ ref('stg_nations') }} n on c.nation_key = n.nation_key
join {{ ref('stg_regions') }} r on n.region_key = r.region_key
patch.explanation: The `unique_dim_customers_customer_key` test failed with 1500 duplicate rows. `stg_customers` has 1500 distinct `customer_key` values, but `dim_customers` contains 7500 rows, indicating each customer was duplicated 5 times. Inspecting `dim_customers` SQL shows an incorrect join: `join {{ ref('stg_regions') }} r on n.region_key = n.region_key`, which is always true and creates a Cartesian product with all regions (5 rows). Changing the join condition to `n.region_key = r.region_key` restores the proper 1‑to‑1 relationship, eliminating duplicate rows and satisfying the uniqueness test.
